summary: Joseph Carlson After Hours gives a fair value (his price target) for every one of his 14 holdings, with the theme that he is holding throughout — several flips below are BUY to HOLD because he is not adding at current prices, not sells. On his own figures the portfolio is about 17% undervalued in aggregate. Mastercard (MA) is an explicit HOLD at fair value near $700 versus $659, with record profits and a wide moat but only modest upside. Amazon (AMZN) is a HOLD at $350 (about 40% upside) — one of the best opportunities today, but not adding because it is already his second-largest position and about 60% of the portfolio sits in four or five names. Alphabet (GOOGL) is a HOLD at $350 (over 20% upside), undervalued but needing to prove ad revenue holds up against AI agents. Meta (META) is a HOLD near $850 (about 40% upside), deeply undervalued on ten-year cash flow, but already over 11% weight. S&P Global (SPGI), Texas Roadhouse (TXRH), Moody's (MCO) and DoorDash (DASH) all flip from BUY to HOLD as their valuation gaps closed. Microsoft (MSFT) is a first-tracked HOLD at $550, close to fair value; ASML a HOLD near $1,800 after trimming 20% near $1,900; Costco (COST) a HOLD near $800 versus $1,000 (about 22% overvalued) though he is very slow to sell. Netflix (NFLX) stays a BUY at about $100 versus $62, Duolingo (DUOL) a cautious first-tracked HOLD near $200 versus $135 ahead of earnings, and Uber (UBER) softens from BUY to CONDITIONAL_BUY at $90 versus $66, likely waiting for earnings before adding.
